generations.purpose: Initial six-pose horizontal secondary sweep; rejected for rectangular cell overlap.
generations.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: transparent six-frame combat animation spritesheet for original industrial miner hero CH01, right mouse secondary attack "pilebreaker sweep".
Input images: Image 1 (CH01_basic_front_v1.png) is the exact character identity, proportions, costume, weapon and camera reference only; its overhead action is NOT the action to copy. Image 2 (CH01_combat_v1.png) is a close visual reference for the SAME character and single hydraulic hammer.
Primary request: draw exactly SIX different consecutive key poses of ONE powerful grounded HORIZONTAL WAIST-HIGH HAMMER SWEEP, in a strict three-columns by two-rows contact sheet read left to right then next row. Landscape 1536x1024. Each complete character, feet, hands and whole hammer contained inside its own 512x512 cell, with ample empty transparent gutters and outer margins. All six have identical camera, fixed anatomical body scale, and coherent two-handed grip. Fixed boot baseline and stance origin within every cell.
Identity: stocky muscular adult man with short black hair, slight beard, orange and coal-black industrial work clothes, ivory scarf and rolled sleeves, black/brown heavy boots, massive grated left shoulder plate, right arm orange piston apparatus with brass fittings and black hoses, amber belt lamp. Preserve the reference's SAME short two-handed orange hydraulic impact hammer/ram with rectangular steel head and two blunt parallel metal pistons, same dimensions in all six frames. No other weapon. Detailed painted 2D game sprite, crisp metal and fabric separation, restrained highlights.
Camera: front three-quarter southeast view from slightly above, face visible, torso and feet directed toward screen RIGHT / lower-right. Do not reverse direction between poses; the runtime will mirror.
Action story:
1 top-left PLANT: low center of gravity, wide grounded stance, both boots firmly planted, hammer held low across pelvis, preparing to pull it back toward the character's rear / screen-left.
2 top-middle COIL: deepest distinct anticipation, knees loaded, hips and waist twisted, both hands pulled back, hammer head LOW BEHIND the hip toward screen-left. The hammer NEVER rises overhead.
3 top-right DRIVE: hips uncoil toward screen-right, hammer passes horizontally at waist level beside the body, arms extending; this is clearly intermediate between the rear loaded pose and contact.
4 bottom-left CONTACT: strongest horizontal extension to screen-right / slightly lower-right, front knee braced, torso drives into the hit, hammer's blunt twin-piston collision face at waist height at the FRONT, both hands visibly supporting one hammer. No impact effect.
5 bottom-middle FOLLOW: continuation of the same horizontal arc, torso rotates farther, hammer carries past the body's front into a cross-body follow-through, bent arms absorbing momentum. Make this a visibly distinct follow-through, not a duplicate of contact.
6 bottom-right READY: bring the single hammer back into the low neutral two-hand carry shown by the combat reference; torso rises, ready to repeat.
Both feet remain grounded in every pose; allow natural foot pivot but no jump, no backward step, no sliding. Keep one fixed standing anatomical body height for the whole sheet; crouched poses are naturally shorter, never magnified to fill cells.
Background: genuine alpha transparency. Avoid text, labels, numbers, grid lines, watermark, floor, environment, baked cast shadows, explosions, particles, speed lines, motion trails, duplicated limbs, weapon ghost images. No overhead swing, no raised weapon, no spear, no gun barrel reinterpretation. Preserve entire weapon and both boot soles with no cropping.

generations.purpose: One targeted correction for cell separation, keeping the same character and poses.

Each complete character AND whole hammer AND both feet MUST fit within the interior of its own cell, leaving at least 32 truly transparent pixels between visible pixels and all four cell edges. In particular top-middle's rearward hammer must not extend into top-left; bottom-left's hammer must not extend into bottom-middle; bottom-middle's hammer and foot must not extend into bottom-right or bottom-left.
Use the SAME UNIFORM REDUCTION of all six figures and weapons together, roughly 0.72 of current source scale, then move each figure as a whole into its cell. Keep fixed anatomical scale across the six sprites. Do not enlarge individual crouches. Center the planted boot midpoint near local (220,430) in EVERY cell and fit weapons around it.
Preserve the six original distinct action poses in order and their detailed appearance exactly: low plant, low behind-the-hip coil, waist-height drive, horizontal contact, horizontal continuation/follow, low ready. This is the same hero and same two-handed short orange rectangular twin-piston hammer. Do not replace any pose, lift hammer overhead, reverse the character's screen-right direction, add limbs, add another weapon, or change costume. Same front three-quarter camera and rendering style.
Background genuinely alpha-transparent. NO ground, shadows, backdrop gradient, effects, particles, labels, text, grid lines, numbers, motion ghosts or borders. Every sprite completely isolated with transparent outer padding.

generations.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: transparent six-frame combat animation spritesheet for original industrial miner hero CH01, right mouse secondary attack "pilebreaker sweep", BACK bank.
Input images: Image 1 (CH01_basic_back_v1.png) is exact BACK VIEW character identity/costume/weapon/camera reference only; do NOT copy the old overhead action. Image 2 (CH01_secondary_front_v1.png) is the exact required six-pose horizontal secondary sweep action and painted style, to recreate from BEHIND.
Primary request: draw exactly SIX different consecutive key poses of ONE powerful grounded HORIZONTAL WAIST-HIGH HAMMER SWEEP, in a strict three-columns by two-rows contact sheet read left to right then next row. Landscape 1536x1024. Six equal 512x512 cells, whole character plus entire weapon kept within each cell with transparent outer padding of at least 32 pixels. Use smaller figures to guarantee separated full silhouettes; do not fill cells edge-to-edge. Constant standing anatomical body height approximately 315 source pixels; crouches naturally lower. Fixed planted boot midpoint around local (235,435) for EVERY cell. All six share camera, scale and stable gear dimensions.
Identity: same stocky muscular adult male, short black hair, orange/coal-black industrial workwear, ivory scarf and rolled sleeves, heavy boots, massive grated left shoulder plate, right arm orange piston apparatus with brass fittings and black hoses, amber belt lamp, brown leather straps over back. Keep the SAME SINGLE short two-handed orange hydraulic hammer/ram with rectangular steel head and two blunt parallel metal pistons from the references. This is a heavy blunt impact tool, not a firearm. Both hands maintain continuous plausible grip. Highly detailed painted 2D game sprite, crisp materials, restrained highlights.
Camera: BACK three-quarter northeast view from slightly above, back of head, back/spine and shoulder grate visible, face hidden; hero and attack directed toward screen RIGHT / UPPER-RIGHT throughout. Never face camera, do not alternate left/right; runtime will mirror.
Six key poses corresponding precisely to the front action:
1 top-left PLANT: wide braced grounded stance, hammer carried low across front pelvis, both boots anchored, preparing rearward twist.
2 top-middle COIL: deepest anticipation, knees loaded, hips and waist rotate against swing, hands and hammer head pulled LOW BEHIND rear hip toward screen-left / lower-left. The hammer NEVER goes overhead.
3 top-right DRIVE: hips uncoil, hammer passes beside the body at waist-height in a HORIZONTAL arc toward screen-right / upper-right. Arms extending, clear intermediate position between rear coil and contact.
4 bottom-left CONTACT: strongest horizontal reach to screen-right / upper-right at waist height, torso rotates into blow and front knee braces. Hammer twin-piston collision face in front of character, wholly visible, no impact effects.
5 bottom-middle FOLLOW: momentum continues the same horizontal arc across the body, shoulder/waist turned farther and bent arms absorb weight, hammer visibly past contact into continuation. Keep this distinct from contact.
6 bottom-right READY: return hammer into same low two-hand neutral carry as the references; torso rises and settles.
Feet grounded throughout, no jump or backstep, no sliding. Natural boot pivot only. Never rescale individual crouches. The front reference's sequence is low-side-coil then horizontal hammer sweep; no overhead or downward slam in this sheet.
Background: ACTUAL TRANSPARENT ALPHA. No painted background, background gradient, glow, ground plane, shadow, scenery, explosion, particles, labels, text, lines, frames, motion trails, speed effects, repeated limbs, repeated weapon ghost. Exactly one head/two arms/two legs/one hammer per cell; all boot soles and whole tool inside cell with generous transparent gutters.

constraints: Only new secondary assets/manifests/provenance and ignored CH01_secondary candidate files were owned by the artwork task.
No Godot execution, import, GPU capture, image compositing, alpha cleanup, resizing, pixel painting, or forged screenshots.
Fixed anatomical body_height per bank; no per-frame rescaling.
Enabled=false until root visual and gameplay-scale acceptance.
Coordinates are absolute source atlas pixels; regions and alpha_bounds are x,y,width,height.
Back follow and ready alpha>8 bounding rectangles overlap horizontally by four source pixels; original PNG preserved and limitation explicitly recorded.
registration_method: Manual landmark placement on generated originals. Independent read-only visual review of back landmarks and front boot sole centers. Read-only alpha connected-component scan and per-region bounds. No pixel output generated by Pillow.
runtime_acceptance: Root enabled both manifests after 138 functional and 89 native checks. All six poses observed for each front/back hit/whiff cast. Actual gameplay screenshots reviewed; see manifest validation and artifacts/hammer_secondary_native/native_capture.json. Six keyposes, not full continuous animation.
limits: Six discrete key poses per bank, not a full interpolated animation or eight-direction art.
Only front/back banks; runtime handles horizontal mirroring.
Back lower-row follow/ready split is provisional and contains a known four-source-column compromise.

provisional_crop_policy.reason: Generated component bounds overlap by four columns. Root selected separate rectangle edges that each clip at most four local source columns, avoiding visible neighboring-pose fragments; native acceptance is managed by root.
